memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt. - Gen 19:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short verse, and one of the saddest in the Bible. Lot's wife had been rescued. She was out of the city, on the path to safety, spared by grace along with her family. But she "looked back" - and she was lost. So near to salvation, and yet her heart betrayed her.

Why did she look back? Because her heart was still in Sodom. The angels had said, "Don't look back." Her backward glance was not mere curiosity; it was longing. Her body had left the city, but her affections had not. She was rescued from Sodom, but Sodom was not rescued from her heart.

This is a solemn warning for every one of us. It is possible to be near salvation, to travel alongside God's people, to be pulled out of danger by grace - and still be lost because our hearts remain attached to what God is saving us from. Outward rescue is not the same as a heart truly turned to God.

Jesus made this verse a permanent warning: "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:32). He was teaching that on the day of His return, we must not cling to this world but be ready to leave it wholly for Him. "Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it" (Luke 17:33). Where is your heart truly fixed? Don't be someone whose feet are following God while their heart looks back with longing at the world.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is your heart fully turned to God, or does it still look back with longing?
- What might you be clinging to that God is calling you to release?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, save me from a divided heart that follows You outwardly while longing for the world. Turn my affections fully to You. Help me remember Lot's wife, and hold nothing back from You.
Amen.
